# test04 — test04_fedavg_3h

## Objective

Three sites: does further fragmentation compound the cost?

## Research question

RQ1 — the shape of degradation as sites increase.

## Hospitals

**3** — 3 hospitals, balanced (33.3 each)  ->  33.3% / 33.3% / 33.3%

## Data split

Patients are divided **by patient, never by slice**: every image of a
patient goes to exactly one hospital, and no patient appears at two sites. Splitting
by slice would let a model recognise the patient rather than the disease.

| hospital | share of training patients | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|
| `hospital_1` | 33.3% | 1 |
| `hospital_2` | 33.3% | 1 |
| `hospital_3` | 33.3% | 1 |

The split is **stratified**: every hospital keeps the global class ratio, so the only thing that varies between them is QUANTITY. This is a deliberate limitation and the dissertation states it — tests 08 and 09 are quantity skew, not genuine non-IID heterogeneity.

Each hospital additionally holds out 20% of
its own patients as a local validation split. That is what produces the metric the
server selects on, and it is local by construction: a hospital cannot validate on
another hospital's patients.

Data lives in `data/partitions/3_clients_balanced/<hospital>/`, written by
`scripts/partition_data.py` and checked by `scripts/verify_data.py`.

## Aggregation algorithm

**FedAvg** (McMahan et al., 2017) — the server averages the client updates, weighting each by how much data that site trained on. The baseline aggregation, and the reference every other one is measured against.

## Protocol

| | |
|---|---|
| rounds x local epochs | 30 x 1 |
| total epochs of data | 30 (budget-matched to the centralised baseline) |
| model selection | `val_balanced_accuracy`, on held-out client patients — never training accuracy |
| model | `resnet18`, ImageNet-pretrained, 3 classes |
| frozen | `layer3` — conv1+bn1+layer1+layer2 (the configuration whose seed spread was 0.003, not 0.026) |
| input | 224x224 RGB, three DCE phases fused |
| optimiser | adamw, lr 0.0001, weight decay 0.0005 |
| regularisation | dropout 0.5, label smoothing 0.1, gradient clip 1.0 |
| batch size | 24, at most 1 slice per patient |
| class weights | inverse frequency per PATIENT, scope `local` |
| seed | 42 |

Every value above comes from `config/experiments.py`. Nothing is set in this folder.

## Run

```bash
python scripts/run_experiment.py test04
```

## What this produces

`results/test04_fedavg_3h/` — the model, `rounds.csv` (one row per round per
hospital), per-patient predictions on the global test set, the resolved
configuration, and the full log. Enough to regenerate every dissertation figure
without re-running anything.

## Evaluation

Reported at **patient level**: slice probabilities are averaged into one prediction
per patient before any metric, because slices of one patient are near-duplicates and
a slice-level score measures patient recognition rather than disease. The headline
metric is one-vs-rest **macro-AUC**. Accuracy is never quoted without the trivial
baseline of the same split beside it.

All nine experiments are scored on the **same global test set**, which no hospital
sees during training.

## Reading the result

The noise floor on this task is **0.067 macro-AUC**, measured between two runs of a
byte-identical configuration differing only in random seed. Treat a smaller
difference as "no difference detected" — that is a finding, and belongs in the
dissertation as one. One seed is not a result.
